name: Tirana
title: Holidays in Tirana
intro: Bright painted blocks, Cold War bunkers turned museums and buzzing café streets in Albania's fast-changing capital, with mountains on its doorstep. Here's what Tirana is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: The clock tower and the minaret and dome of the Et'hem Bey Mosque beside Skanderbeg Square in central Tirana

facts.label: Entry
facts.value: No visa for up to 90 days

facts_note: Albania isn't in the EU and uses the lek. Some hotels take euros, but carry lek for taxis, markets and small cafés. Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: May, June and September are the best months, warm enough for café terraces and the cable car without the heat of high summer. July and August often pass 30°C, and many locals head to the coast. Winters are mild but wet, with November usually the rainiest month.

things.name: Skanderbeg Square
things.blurb: The huge main square, ringed by the National History Museum, the opera house, the clock tower and the Et'hem Bey Mosque.

things.name: Bunk'Art 2
things.blurb: A museum in a Cold War bunker in the centre, telling the story of the communist-era secret police.

things.name: Bunk'Art 1
things.blurb: A much larger bunker on the edge of the city, built for the leadership, with rooms of exhibits deep under the hill.

things.name: Pyramid of Tirana
things.blurb: Built as a memorial to the dictator Enver Hoxha, now covered in street art with steps you can climb for views.

things.name: Blloku
things.blurb: Once closed to everyone but the communist elite, now the city's liveliest area for cafés, bars and restaurants.

things.name: Dajti Ekspres
things.blurb: A cable car from the edge of the city up Mount Dajti, with big views and walks at the top. Check the opening days before you go.

things.name: New Bazaar (Pazari i Ri)
things.blurb: A covered market and surrounding streets with fruit, cheese, olives and good, cheap places to eat.

faqs.question: How do you get to Tirana from the UK?
faqs.answer: Fly direct. British Airways flies from Heathrow, and Ryanair started flights from Birmingham in 2026. The flight takes about three hours.

faqs.question: Is Tirana worth visiting?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's lively, cheap and unlike any other European capital, with fascinating Cold War history and easy day trips to Berat and the mountains.

faqs.question: How many days do you need in Tirana?
faqs.answer: Two or three days covers the main sights and the cable car. Add more if you want to travel on to Berat or the coast.

faqs.question: Can you use euros in Tirana?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, mainly in hotels and some restaurants, but you'll get a worse rate and change in lek. It's easier to pay in lek or by card.
